title: Shira Route vs Lemosho: What Is the Difference?
excerpt: Shira and Lemosho both cross the Shira Plateau. The difference is where they start, and that has consequences for acclimatisation.
body:
On paper the Shira and Lemosho routes look almost the same: both start on the western side and both cross the Shira Plateau. The difference is the starting point.

## Shira starts higher

The Shira Route starts at around 3,600 m, reached by car on a track to the Shira Plateau. Lemosho starts lower, in the forest at around 2,100 m, and reaches the plateau on foot.

That sounds like an advantage for Shira: less walking. But starting at 3,600 m means your body goes from city altitude to mountain altitude in a few hours. Many people get a headache the first night on Shira.

## Lemosho walks there

Lemosho takes one or two extra days to reach the same point, but your body adapts step by step. That is why most operators, including our partner, now prefer Lemosho over Shira.

## When Shira can make sense

- If you have already been at altitude recently, for example after climbing [Mount Meru](/blog/mount-meru-climb-guide/).
- If walking through the forest is less important to you.

## From the plateau onwards

From Shira Camp both routes continue identically: Lava Tower, Barranco, Karanga, Barafu and the summit.

## Our advice

For most climbers, Lemosho is the better choice. Read our [Lemosho guide](/blog/kilimanjaro-lemosho-route-guide/) or compare all routes in [Which Kilimanjaro route is right for you?](/blog/best-kilimanjaro-route-for-you/).
